weeks.title: Proper 23
weeks.intro: The Gospel is the parable of the wedding banquet, a difficult text in which a king's invited guests refuse to come, those who do come include a man not dressed appropriately, and the king has him thrown out. The Old Testament reading is the golden calf episode, including the remarkable scene of Moses interceding for the people and changing God's mind. The Epistle includes Paul's "rejoice in the Lord always" and the catalog of what to think about ("whatever is true, whatever is honorable"). The Psalm rehearses Israel's long pattern of forgetfulness.

weeks.title: Proper 24
weeks.intro: The Gospel is the "give to Caesar what is Caesar's" exchange, in which Jesus deflects a trap question about Roman taxes. The Old Testament reading is Moses asking to see God's glory, and God hiding Moses in the cleft of the rock while passing by. The Epistle opens Paul's first letter to the Thessalonians with extended thanksgiving for their faith. The Psalm is a hymn to God's holy reign.

weeks.title: Proper 25
weeks.intro: The Gospel is the greatest commandment exchange, in which Jesus consolidates the whole of the law into love of God and love of neighbor. The Old Testament reading is the death of Moses on Mount Nebo. The Epistle is Paul recalling his pastoral conduct among the Thessalonians. The Psalm is the great psalm of mortality and time ("a thousand years in your sight are like yesterday").

weeks.title: All Saints
weeks.intro: All Saints falls on a Sunday this year, and the lectionary sets aside the ordinary readings for it. The Gospel is the Beatitudes. The first reading is Revelation's vision of the great multitude no one could count, from every nation and tribe, gathered before the throne. The Epistle is 1 John's astonishing claim that we are God's children now, and that what we will be has not yet been revealed. The Psalm invites the congregation to taste and see that the Lord is good.

weeks.title: Proper 27
weeks.intro: The Gospel is the parable of the ten bridesmaids, half of whom run out of oil waiting for a bridegroom who is later than anyone expected. The Old Testament reading is Joshua gathering the tribes at Shechem for covenant renewal: "choose this day whom you will serve." The Epistle is Paul's word to the Thessalonians about grieving with hope. The Psalm is Psalm 78:1-7, the resolve to tell the coming generation.

weeks.title: Proper 28
weeks.intro: The Gospel is the parable of the talents, in which two servants put their master's money to work and a third buries his in the ground out of fear. The Old Testament reading introduces Deborah, prophet and judge, summoning Barak to a fight he does not want to lead alone. The Epistle calls the Thessalonians children of the day who encourage one another and build each other up. The Psalm lifts its eyes to God the way a servant watches the hand of a master.

weeks.title: Reign of Christ
weeks.intro: The last Sunday before Advent. The Gospel is the judgment of the nations, where the king turns out to have been present in the least of these all along. Ezekiel pictures God as the shepherd who seeks out the lost and judges between the fat sheep and the lean. The Epistle prays that the church will know the hope of its calling and the power of the risen Christ. The Psalm calls all the earth to enter God's gates with thanksgiving.
